> **Key takeaways**
> - Parents can only book class times that exist. A schedule that ends is a class that stops filling.
> - Families plan weeks ahead, so publish at least a month or two of sessions at a time.
> - Keep the same day and time every week; it is easier to fit into a family calendar.
> - On ORYN Quest, **Keep repeating** adds new weekly sessions for you, so there are always about eight weeks ahead to book.

## The quiet reason a full class goes empty

Plenty of studios, coaches and tutors know this feeling. A class fills nicely for a few weeks, then new bookings slow down and eventually stop. It is easy to blame the season, the price or the competition.

Very often the reason is simpler: **the schedule ran out.** A parent who finds your class in mid-October and sees only two more sessions, or none at all, has nothing to book. They move on to a class that shows them the next two months.

That is especially true online. A parent browsing on a phone at 9 p.m. is not going to message you to ask whether there will be classes in November. If the dates are not on the page, the class looks finished.

## Why families need to see weeks ahead

Kids' activities are planned around everything else: school, carpools, siblings, work shifts and weekend sports. Parents usually decide a few weeks out, and they want to know that a class will still be there once their child settles in.

A visible run of upcoming sessions does three things:

- **It answers "is this still running?"** without anyone having to ask.
- **It lets parents pick a start date that works**, instead of a date that happens to be next.
- **It makes a weekly habit easy.** The same day and time every week fits neatly into a family calendar, and repeat families are the backbone of a steady class.

## Keep the same day and time

Consistency is a feature. A class that moves from Tuesday at 4:30 to Thursday at 5:00 and back again forces every family to re-plan. A class that is always Saturday at 10:00 becomes part of the week.

If you need to skip a holiday, cancel that one session rather than reshuffling the whole pattern. Families on ORYN Quest get all their credits back when the vendor cancels a session, so a skipped week is easy to handle. Keep it to real exceptions, though: frequent cancelling can hurt how your class ranks.

## How Keep repeating works on ORYN Quest

On ORYN Quest you can add class times one at a time, or set up a whole term at once from a repeating pattern: weekly, every two weeks or monthly.

For a class that simply runs every week, there is now an easier option: **Keep repeating**.

- When you set up your first class in **Get your class live**, the box **Keep repeating after that** is ticked for you.
- On your **Schedule** page, when you create a repeating term, you can tick **Keep repeating after the term ends**.
- With it on, ORYN adds new weekly sessions for you, so families always see about **eight weeks** of upcoming class times. A daily job tops the schedule up; you don't have to remember to.
- You can stop repeating whenever you like. Sessions families already booked stay exactly as they are.

It is the difference between a class that quietly runs dry in week nine and a class that is always open for the next family.

## A quick schedule check you can do today

Open your class listing and look at it the way a parent would:

1. **Count the upcoming sessions.** Fewer than four? Families may assume it is ending.
2. **Check the pattern.** Same day, same time? If not, can it be?
3. **Look past the holidays.** Is there anything after Thanksgiving and the winter break, when families plan their January?
4. **Turn on Keep repeating** for any class that runs every week.

## FAQ

### Why did bookings for my kids' class stop?

A common and easy-to-miss reason is that the schedule ran out: parents can only book class times that exist. Check how many upcoming sessions your listing shows. If there are only a few, publish more or turn on Keep repeating.

### How far ahead should I publish class times?

At least a month, and ideally about two. Families plan around school and other activities and often decide a few weeks in advance. On ORYN Quest, Keep repeating keeps about eight weeks of weekly sessions open to book.

### Can I stop a repeating class?

Yes. You can stop repeating at any time from your schedule. Sessions families have already booked are not changed.

### What if I need to skip one week?

Cancel that single session instead of changing the whole pattern. When a vendor cancels a session on ORYN Quest, families get all of their credits back.
